claim: High levels of GALNT relocation (GALA) are found in a majority of samples from malignant tumors.
source: High levels of relocation or GALA are found in a majority of samples from malignant tumors.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A which shows correlation between GALNT relocation and Tn levels in solid tumors.

claim: Most cancer cell lines in vitro show limited levels of GALA.
source: By contrast and for unknown reasons, most cancer cell lines in vitro show limited levels of GALA (Gill et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gill et al., 2013.

claim: Src8A7F is a mostly inactive kinase that can be chemically rescued and activated by imidazole.
source: The Cole group has demonstrated that a mutant form of Src, Src(R388A,Y527F) or Src8A7F for short, is a mostly inactive kinase that can be chemically rescued and activated by imidazole (Qiao et al., 2006; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Qiao et al., 2006 and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Imidazole treatment of HeLa-IS cells induces a twofold increase in total Tn levels after 2 hr.
source: In terms of GALA, imidazole treatment induced a twofold increase in total Tn levels after 2 hr with a pattern of Tn staining a mix of Golgi and ER, suggesting a measured GALNT relocation (Figure 1B and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Imidazole treatment in wild-type HeLa cells had no effect on Tn.
source: Imidazole treatment in wild-type HeLa cells had no effect on Tn (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Imidazole washout after 24 hr of treatment results in a significant reduction of Tn levels within 1 hr.
source: We also observed that the effects of Src8A7F activation were reversible: imidazole washout after 24 hr of treatment resulted in a significant reduction of Tn levels within 1 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Stimulation with 50 ng/ml PDGF yields around a twofold increase in total Tn levels.
source: Stimulation with 50 ng/ml PDGF yielded around a twofold increase in total Tn levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H and I), similar to that observed with imidazole treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H and I.

claim: Imidazole stimulation of HEK-IS cells results in a fivefold increase of PDIA4 glycosylation after 4 hr.
source: We measured the effects of Src8A7F imidazole rescue on the glycosylation of PDIA4 using VVL immunoprecipitation (IP) followed by PDIA4 blotting and quantified a fivefold increase of PDIA4 glycosylation after 4 hr (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: GFP-positive tubules start to emanate from the Golgi as soon as 10 min after imidazole stimulation.
source: Upon imidazole addition, GFP-positive tubules started to emanate from the Golgi as soon as 10 min after stimulation, their numbers reaching peak around 20–30 min, then decreasing to slightly above unstimulated conditions (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E and F, and Figure 1—video 1.

claim: GALNT2 tubules are deprived of the peripheral Golgi protein Giantin.
source: The tubules were deprived of the peripheral Golgi protein Giantin (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: GALNT2 tubules are deprived of the chimeric Golgi enzyme beta 1,4-galactosyltransferase (GALT) tagged with mCherry.
source: In addition, they appeared deprived of the chimeric Golgi enzyme beta 1,4-galactosyltransferase (GALT) tagged with mCherry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Src activation results in a mild reduction of COPI intensity at the Golgi between 5 and 20 min.
source: Surprisingly, using both high-resolution microscopy and quantitative automated high-throughput confocal microscopy, we observed no increase but instead a mild reduction of COPI intensity at the Golgi between 5 and 20 min after Src activation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–N.

claim: siRNA knockdown of Arf1 results in a significant reduction of Tn levels upon imidazole treatment.
source: Consistently, siRNA knockdown of Arf1 resulted in a significant reduction of Tn levels upon imidazole treatment and Arf3 knockdown had little effect (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Arf3 knockdown has little effect on Tn levels upon imidazole treatment.
source: Consistently, siRNA knockdown of Arf1 resulted in a significant reduction of Tn levels upon imidazole treatment and Arf3 knockdown had little effect (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Arf1-V5 localizes on GALNT2 tubules upon Src8A7F activation.
source: Upon Src8A7F activation, Arf1-V5 appeared to be recruited at the Golgi and localized on the GALNT2 tubules, almost throughout the structure (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Arf1 membrane-association increases within 5 min of Src activation, peaks at 10 min, and begins to fall after 20 min.
source: To confirm the membrane recruitment of Arf1, we isolated cytosolic and membrane proteins to measure the levels of membrane-bound Arf1 and found Arf1 membrane-association increased within 5 min, peaked at 10 min, and began to fall after 20 min while the cytosolic pool remained relatively constant (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Arf1-GTP levels increase more than twofold within 5 min of imidazole induction in HEK-IS cells.
source: Strikingly, Arf1-GTP levels increased more than twofold within 5 min of imidazole induction (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Arf1-GTP levels subside after 30 min of stimulation despite continuous Src activity.
source: Interestingly, Arf1-GTP levels subsided after 30 min of stimulation despite continuous Src activity.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of Arf1-GTP levels over time.

claim: Transient expression of SrcEG for 18 hr results in a marked decrease in the amount of Arf1-GTP.
source: Surprisingly, transient expression of SrcEG for 18 hr resulted in a marked decrease in the amount of Arf1-GTP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: GBF1 RNAi-mediated knockdown results in a significant reduction of Tn levels following Src activation in HEK-IS cells.
source: Following Src activation in imidazole-treated HEK-IS, GBF1 RNAi-mediated knockdown resulted similarly in a significant reduction of Tn levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) and PDIA4 glycosylation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Expression of GFP-GBF1 alone enhances Arf1-GTP levels in HEK-IS.
source: Expression of a GFP-tagged form of GBF1 (GFP-GBF1) alone enhances Arf1-GTP levels in HEK-IS (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Upon imidazole stimulation, GFP-GBF1 expression increases Arf1-GTP loading by nearly threefold within 10 min.
source: Strikingly, upon imidazole stimulation, GTP loading was further increased by nearly threefold within 10 min of induction (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: GBF1 knockdown prevents significant Arf-GTP production after imidazole stimulation.
source: In these conditions, GBF1 levels were already significantly lowered; imidazole stimulation did not result in significant Arf-GTP production (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: GBF1 knockdown results in over 90% reduction of Arf activation after Src stimulation.
source: Averaging three independent experiments resulted in over 90% reduction of Arf activation (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The GBF1 membrane pool in HEK-IS increases by roughly threefold within 5–10 min of imidazole treatment.
source: Strikingly, the GBF1 membrane pool in HEK-IS increased by roughly threefold within 5–10 min, while total GBF1 remained constant.
evidence: The claim is based on biochemical fractionation data.

claim: GBF1 Golgi levels increase rapidly after imidazole treatment, peaking at ~10 min.
source: In sync with the biochemical experiment, GBF1 Golgi levels increased rapidly, peaking at ~10 min, decreasing after ~20 min but not to baseline levels (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Phosphorylated GBF1 displays increased binding to Arf1-V5 compared to non-phosphorylated GBF1.
source: By comparison with inactive SrcKM, SrcEG induced a twofold increase in binding (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Phosphorylated GBF1 displays increased binding to purified Arf1-del17-His.
source: As with Arf1-V5, phosphorylated GBF1 displayed increased binding to purified Arf1-del17-His (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: GBF1 depletion almost completely prevents tubule formation after imidazole stimulation.
source: After imidazole stimulation, control cells displayed abundant tubule formation while tubules were almost nonexistent in GBF1-depleted cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G and H, Figure 3—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G and H, and Figure 3—videos 1 and 2.

claim: GBF1 tyrosine phosphorylation increases within 5 min of imidazole stimulation and is sustained for 2 hr.
source: After imidazole stimulation of HEK-IS cells, GBF1 was immunoprecipitated and probed with an antibody specific for tyrosine phosphorylation, revealing an increase within 5 min that was sustained for 2 hr (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: NIH3T3vSrc cells display four times as much phospho-GBF1 as normal NIH3T3 cells.
source: They also display four times as much phospho-GBF1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: GBF1 is a direct substrate of Src.
source: In the presence of ATP, GFP-GBF1 displayed marked phosphotyrosine levels compared to controls, indicating that GBF1 is a direct substrate of Src (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro phosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Src phosphorylates GBF1 on 10 tyrosine residues.
source: Phosphopeptides were analyzed with tandem mass spectrometry, revealing 10 phosphorylated tyrosine residues with high confidence (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Y876 is conserved in GBF1 homologues in various species.
source: A database search revealed that Y876 is conserved in GBF1 homologues in various species (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Y898 is conserved in GBF1 in most species.
source: Y898 is also conserved in GBF1 in most species (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Multiple GEFs can be phosphorylated on the tyrosine analogous to Y876.
source: Interestingly, a search on PhosphoSitePlus database indicates that multiple GEFs, including Brefeldin-Resistant Arf-GEF 2 (BRAG2, IQSEC1), Brefeldin A-Inhibited Guanine Nucleotide-Exchange Protein 1 (BIG1), and Cytohesin 2 (ARNO), can be phosphorylated on the tyrosine analogous to Y876 (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by database search results shown in Figure 4H.

claim: GBF1 displays about 180-fold increase in phosphorylated Y876 peptide in the presence of SrcEG compared to SrcKM.
source: GBF1, in the presence of SrcEG, displayed about 180-fold increase in phosphorylated Y876 peptide (DFEQDILEDMyHAIK) and 100-fold in increase in phosphorylated Y898 peptide (ENyVWNVLLHR) compared to SrcKM-expressing samples, suggesting that these sites are the major phosphorylation targets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by SILAC mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H.

claim: GBF1 displays about 100-fold increase in phosphorylated Y898 peptide in the presence of SrcEG compared to SrcKM.
source: GBF1, in the presence of SrcEG, displayed about 180-fold increase in phosphorylated Y876 peptide (DFEQDILEDMyHAIK) and 100-fold in increase in phosphorylated Y898 peptide (ENyVWNVLLHR) compared to SrcKM-expressing samples, suggesting that these sites are the major phosphorylation targets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by SILAC mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H.

claim: The 2P4 antibody is specific for phospho-Y876 on GBF1.
source: While wild-type GBF1 showed strong reactivity and total phosphotyrosine levels were moderately affected, the band was completely abolished in the Y876F mutant (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4I demonstrating loss of signal with Y876F mutant.

claim: Phospho-Y876 is detected within 5 min of imidazole treatment and persists for 2 hr.
source: Similarly to overall phosphotyrosine levels, phospho-Y876 was detected within 5 min of imidazole treatment and persisted for 2 hr (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Y876 is a direct target of Src.
source: We also verified that Y876 is a direct target of Src using the in vitro phosphorylation assay (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro phosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4K and Figure 4—figure supplement 1K.

claim: PDGF stimulation of HeLa cells induces phosphorylation of GBF1 at Y876.
source: Starting with serum-starved HeLa cells stimulated with PDGF, endogenous GBF1 was immunoprecipitated and phospho-Y876 found to display similar kinetics to generic GBF1 tyrosine phosphorylation (Figure 4L).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: EGF stimulation of A431 cells induces phosphorylation of GBF1 at Y876 within 10–20 min.
source: A431 cells, which express high levels of EGFR, were stimulated with 100 ng/ml of EGF (Fernandez-Pol, 1985). Similarly to PDGF with HeLa cells, phospho-Y876 was upregulated within 10–20 min (Figure 4M).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4M and citation to Fernandez-Pol, 1985.

claim: The Y876F mutant abolishes Arf1-GTP increase after Src8A7F activation.
source: This increase was abolished with the Y876F and double mutant, while residual activation was observed with the Y898F mutant (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: The Y876.898F double mutant reduces basal Arf1-GTP levels.
source: Expression of the double mutant even reduced the basal Arf1-GTP levels.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of Arf1-GTP levels with the double mutant.

claim: GBF1-Y876F and GBF1-Y898F significantly repress Tn levels in SrcEG-expressing cells.
source: GBF1-Y876F or GBF1-Y898F significantly repressed Tn levels in SrcEG-expressing cells (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Single mutants of Y876 or Y898 reduce Arf1 binding by 40 and 60%, respectively.
source: In the in vitro binding assay with purified Arf1-del17 and immuno-purified GFP-GBF1 wild-type and phospho-defective proteins, single mutants of Y876 or Y898 had reduced Arf1 binding by 40 and 60%, respectively, with more than 70% for the double mutant (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: The Y876.898F double mutant reduces Arf1 binding by more than 70%.
source: In the in vitro binding assay with purified Arf1-del17 and immuno-purified GFP-GBF1 wild-type and phospho-defective proteins, single mutants of Y876 or Y898 had reduced Arf1 binding by 40 and 60%, respectively, with more than 70% for the double mutant (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Long-term expression of phosphomimetic GBF1 mutant reduces basal GTP loading levels by more than 70%.
source: First, we observed that after 24 hr overexpression, we observed a reduction of basal GTP loading levels by more than 70% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Cells expressing the Y876.898E mutant show a high incidence of tubule formation.
source: Remarkably, cells expressing the YE mutant showed a high incidence of tubule formation, while cells expressing wild-type GBF1 (GBF1 WT) displayed very little (Figure 5G and H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F, Figure 5—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5G and H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F, and Figure 5—videos 1 and 2.

claim: YE mutant cells display a fivefold higher rate of tubule formation per minute compared to WT GBF1.
source: YE mutant cells displayed a fivefold higher rate of tubule formation per minute of imaging compared to their WT counterpart (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Expression of phosphomimetic mutants of GBF1 results in a mild but significant increase in Tn levels.
source: Expression of the phosphomimetic mutants of GBF1 also resulted in a mild but significant increase in Tn levels in cells transfected with YE mutants compared to GBF1 WT cells (Figure 5I and J), indicating GALNT relocation to the ER.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5I and J.

claim: Y876 phosphorylation induces partial melting of an alpha-helix in Sec7d.
source: As supported by additional mutants, Y876 phosphorylation induces partial melting of an alpha-helix in Sec7d, increasing binding affinity to Arf1.
evidence: The claim is based on molecular modeling and mutagenesis data.

claim: Y898 phosphorylation releases an interaction between Sec7d and the linker domain in C-terminal.
source: Y898 phosphorylation appears to release an interaction between Sec7d and the linker domain in C-terminal.
evidence: The claim is based on molecular modeling.

claim: Molecular dynamics reveals repulsion of the linker away from Sec7d after Y898 phosphorylation.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) revealed a repulsion of the linker away from Sec7d after phosphorylation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and Figure 6—video 1.

claim: Y876 phosphorylation leads to partial unwinding of helix H.
source: When we simulated Y876 phosphorylation, the negative charge was attracted by the positively charged residues arginine 843 (R843) and lysine 844 (K844) at the end of helix H. This, in turn, led to a partial unwinding of helix H, leading to an extension of the loop between helices H and I (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Partial unfolding and loop extension results in better bond formation between Sec7d and Arf1.
source: This partial unfolding and loop extension would result in better bond formation between Sec7d and Arf1 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular modeling shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Y876 phosphorylation results in reduced free binding energy between GBF1 and Arf1.
source: This translates into a reduced free binding energy (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B) and an increased probability of buried surface area (BSA) between the Sec7d and Arf1 (Figure 6D) in the phosphorylated state.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Y876 phosphorylation results in increased probability of buried surface area between Sec7d and Arf1.
source: This translates into a reduced free binding energy (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B) and an increased probability of buried surface area (BSA) between the Sec7d and Arf1 (Figure 6D) in the phosphorylated state.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The R843E.K844E mutant results in a massive reduction in basal cellular Arf1-GTP levels by about 90%.
source: The introduction of negative charges in the R843E.K844E mutant resulted in a massive reduction in basal cellular Arf1-GTP levels by about 90% (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6E and F.

claim: The R843A.K844A mutant does not affect basal Arf1-GTP levels.
source: On the other hand, the mutant with neutral charges (R843A.K844A) did not have an effect on the basal Arf1-GTP levels.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of Arf1-GTP levels with the R843A.K844A mutant.

claim: Cells expressing the R843A.K844A mutant do not upregulate Arf1 GTP loading after Src8A7F stimulation.
source: However, when we stimulated Src8A7F with imidazole, the cells expressing the R843A.K844A mutant did not upregulate Arf1 GTP loading (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6E and F.

claim: The HI loop mutants (both E and A) are insensitive to SrcEG in terms of enhanced binding to Arf1-GDP.
source: As expected, we found that the mutants (both E and A) were insensitive to SrcEG in terms of enhanced binding to Arf1-GDP (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The HI loop mutants result in a significant reduction in Tn levels in cells coexpressing SrcEG.
source: The HI loop mutants resulted in a significant reduction in Tn levels, at levels similar to GBF1-Y876F Figure 6—figure supplement 2C and D.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: Src phosphorylates GBF1 on multiple tyrosines, resulting in extrusion of GALNTs from Golgi membranes in tubules.
source: Here, we propose a model where Src phosphorylates GBF1 on multiple tyrosines, which results in an extrusion of GALNTs from Golgi membranes in tubules and eventually their relocation to the ER (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the study's findings presented in Figure 7A.

claim: The two phosphorylation sites at and near the Sec 7 domain of GBF1 increase its affinity for Arf-GDP.
source: The two phosphorylation sites at and near the Sec 7 domain of GBF1 increase its affinity for Arf-GDP (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is a summary of the study's findings presented in Figure 7B.

claim: Src increases the rate of retrograde traffic of GALNTs through the phosphorylation of GBF1 and regulation of the GBF1-Arf interaction.
source: Thus, Src increases the rate of retrograde traffic of GALNTs through the phosphorylation of GBF1 and regulation of the GBF1-Arf interaction.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: GBF1 is a relatively low abundance protein, almost 50 times less abundant than Arf1.
source: This is partly because GBF1 protein levels are relatively low, almost 50 times less abundant than Arf1 (Itzhak et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Itzhak et al., 2016.

claim: GBF1 is an unstable protein.
source: In addition, others have reported that GBF1 is an unstable protein, which we have also observed with recombinant GBF1 (Bhatt et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bhatt et al., 2016 and the authors' own observations.

claim: Y876 is conserved in all the Sec7d proteins examined.
source: Y876 is conserved in all the Sec7d proteins we looked at.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis.

claim: Phosphorylation of the residue corresponding to Y876 has been reported for several other GEFs in high-throughput databases.
source: For several other GEFs, phosphorylation of the corresponding residue has been reported in various high-throughput databases.
evidence: The claim is based on database searches.

claim: Helix melting regulation by tyrosine phosphorylation could be a widespread mechanism for tyrosine kinases to regulate the GEF family of proteins.
source: These findings suggest that the helix melting regulation is shared by other GEF proteins and could be a widespread mechanism for tyrosine kinases to regulate the GEF family of proteins.
evidence: The claim is a speculative conclusion based on conservation analysis and database searches.

claim: Y898 residue is highly conserved among vertebrates and invertebrates homologues of GBF1.
source: Y898 residue is highly conserved among vertebrates and invertebrates homologues of GBF1, suggesting that its phosphorylation is an ancient, conserved mechanism of regulation.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: The tubules are individually transient but extended, often measuring several micrometers long.
source: The tubules are individually transient but extended, often measuring several micrometers long.
evidence: The claim is based on microscopy observations.

claim: GALNTs relocation is mediated by tubular transport carriers.
source: The data thus suggest that GALNTs relocation is mediated by tubular transport carriers.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on microscopy observations.

claim: The GBF1/Arf1 complex has been shown to interact with the microtubule motor Miro at mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, the GBF1/Arf1 complex has been shown to interact with the microtubule motor Miro at mitochondria (Walch et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Walch et al., 2018.

claim: The Src-GBF1-Arf axis might be involved in the regulation of Golgi organization.
source: The axis Src-GBF1-Arf might also be involved in the regulation of Golgi organization based on the work by Luini's group (Consoli et al., 2012; Luini and Parashuraman, 2016; Pulvirenti et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Consoli et al., 2012; Luini and Parashuraman, 2016; Pulvirenti et al., 2008.

claim: GBF1-Arf are involved in the positioning of mitochondria.
source: GBF1-Arf are also involved in the positioning of mitochondria, a locale where Src kinase has also been detected (Ackema et al., 2014; Hebert-Chatelain, 2013; Walch et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ackema et al., 2014; Hebert-Chatelain, 2013; Walch et al., 2018.

claim: Phosphorylation may regulate the KD for GBF1-Arf binding without affecting the kcat for nucleotide exchange.
source: Phosphorylation might regulate the KD without affecting the kcat.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: Overexpression of GBF1 alone increases Arf-GTP levels, indicating that GBF1 is a limiting factor.
source: To note, overexpression of GBF1 alone increases Arf-GTP levels, indicating that GBF1 is a limiting factor and supporting the idea that an increase in affinity would result in higher Arf-GTP level.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations and inference.

claim: The limiting factor for sustained Arf1-GTP production may arise from the export of GALNTs-containing carriers, resulting in depletion of an unidentified receptor on Golgi membranes.
source: The limiting factor may arise from the export of GALNTs-containing carriers, resulting in the depletion of an unidentified receptor on Golgi membranes.
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the transient nature of Arf1-GTP increase.

claim: Two candidate receptors for Arf-GDP binding to Golgi membranes are the p23 protein and the SNARE membrin.
source: Two candidates have even been proposed, the p23 protein and the SNARE membrin (Gommel et al., 2001; Honda et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gommel et al., 2001 and Honda et al., 2005.

claim: GBF1 requires an additional receptor to bind efficiently to Golgi membranes.
source: GBF1 also appears to require an additional receptor to bind efficiently to Golgi membranes (Quilty et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Quilty et al., 2018.

claim: After Src activation, either the Arf-GDP receptor or the GBF1 receptor (or both) may be transported from Golgi membranes by tubules-derived carriers.
source: It is possible that after Src activation either of these receptors (or both) are transported from Golgi membranes by the tubules-derived carriers.
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the transient nature of Arf1-GTP increase.

claim: Wild-type GBF1 overexpression does not promote GALNTs relocation and thus would not induce receptor depletion.
source: By contrast, wild-type GBF1 overexpression, not promoting GALNTs relocation, would not induce this depletion and can thus stably increase Arf-GTP levels.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed differences between wild-type and phosphomimetic GBF1.

claim: GBF1 binding to Arf-GDP plays a driving role in the formation of transport carriers.
source: It suggests that GBF1 binding to Arf-GDP plays a driving role in the formation of transport carriers.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: The GALA pathway is strongly activated in breast, lung, and liver cancers.
source: This GALNTs Activation (GALA) pathway is strongly activated in breast, lung, and liver cancers and presumably in most high Tn-expressing tumors.
evidence: The claim is stated as an established fact.

claim: GALA markedly promotes tumor growth and metastasis.
source: GALA markedly promotes tumor growth and metastasis (Gill et al., 2013; Nguyen et al., 2017; Ros et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gill et al., 2013; Nguyen et al., 2017; Ros et al., 2020.

claim: GALA is likely an important mediator of Src oncogenic effects.
source: Src has long been implicated in tumorigenesis and tumor invasiveness, and GALA is likely an important mediator of Src oncogenic effects (Chia et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chia et al., 2019 and represents an inference.

claim: GALNTs relocation involves the Arf1 small GTPase.
source: It is unclear how Src stimulates the transport of GALNTs from the Golgi to the ER apart from the fact that the process involves the Arf1 small GTPase and can be blocked by a dominant negative form of Arf1 (Gill et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gill et al., 2010.

claim: GALNTs relocation can be blocked by a dominant negative form of Arf1.
source: It is unclear how Src stimulates the transport of GALNTs from the Golgi to the ER apart from the fact that the process involves the Arf1 small GTPase and can be blocked by a dominant negative form of Arf1 (Gill et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gill et al., 2010.

claim: GBF1 functions at the early cis-Golgi and ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC).
